lede: The biggest thing happening this week is Tuesday's Telluride Town Council meeting, where a public hearing on a vesting period extension and a work session on automated license plate reader cameras — technology that tends to split communities on privacy grounds — are both on the table. Over in Ouray, the city and county are sitting down Monday to work through a draft intergovernmental agreement that would hand full law enforcement for the city over to the Sheriff starting January 1. San Miguel County's BOCC and Planning Commission are also deep in it midweek, with public hearings on affordable housing fee waivers and an active affordable housing code update in progress.
